body: The brain and spinal cord form the central nervous system. Nerves connect it to much of the body. Neurons convey signals through changes in electrical activity and often communicate with other cells using chemical signals. These networks support movement, coordination and the processing of information.

Receptor cells respond to particular kinds of input. Cells in the retina respond to light. Vibrations transmitted through the ear can move sensory cells in the inner ear and produce signals. Other receptors respond to mechanical force, chemicals or temperature. Signals from many receptors are combined during perception.

limitations: The eye photograph shows an external part of the eye. The ear record depicts a model and the microscopy record shows rat neurons. Human sensory experience and abilities vary.
